newsitem.title: SWEDEN: HOW MANY ENTER EMU WILL BE CRUCIAL FOR SWEDEN.
newsitem.headline: HOW MANY ENTER EMU WILL BE CRUCIAL FOR SWEDEN.

text.p: The number of countries which enter Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) could be crucial for Sweden, according to Professor Lars Calmfors, head of a government commission on the subject.
The panel concluded this month that the arguments against Sweden joining in 1991 slightly outweighed those in favour.
But Calmfors said on Friday: "It would not take much to tip the balance. If it were only Sweden and Greece that did not join, it would be hard for Sweden to stay out in the long run."
He told a Centre Party seminar that the most decisive factor in the EMU debate was the attitude of German voters.
"What will decide the whole thing is whether German public opinion is prepared to let go of its mark," he said.
